intent.actor: a person typing successive search queries while earlier responses are in flight
intent.observableSuccess: the list shows the latest request's results and never an older request's late results
intent.nonGoals: cancellation, retry, duplicate responses, debouncing, real network or browser behavior
intent.worstRegression: an older request's late response replaces or briefly precedes the latest results

openQuestions.text: Does one request-id sequence outlive a remount of the search box? Recommended: no claim in this fixture — S1 describes one reducer lifetime, so a response that outlives its search box is owned by the component that mounts it (owner-lifetime), not by this policy

Is anything outside the reducer in scope — the layer that sends requests and tags each response with its id (errors, timeouts, the id a response carries) or the view that renders the list (loading states, counts, labels)? Recommended: no claim in this fixture — S1 describes responses that carry results and says nothing of errors or rendering, and the product under test is the reducer, judged on the events it receives

requirements.quote: Every search request gets a request id that grows by one per issued request.
Issuing a request makes it the latest one; the list keeps showing what it showed until a response arrives.
A response to an older request does not change what the list shows.
The latest request's response is shown when it arrives.
The environment delivers each response at most once, only after its request, in any order.
Cancellation, retry, duplicate responses and a response before its request are out of scope; no guarantee is claimed for them.

policies.text: Issuing a search request makes it the latest request; the list keeps what it shows until a response arrives.
A response to an older request does not alter what the list shows, at any step.
The latest request's response is shown when it arrives.

terms.name: response arrival order
terms.path: test: the world adapter delivers response 1 before request 2 is issued, or after it and before or after response 2
terms.definition: when response 1 arrives: after both requests were issued and before response 2 (OldFirst), after response 2 (NewFirst), or before request 2 is issued (OldEarly)
terms.not: the order in which the requests were issued

terms.name: newer answer arrives
terms.path: test: the world adapter delivers or withholds response 2 within the attempt
terms.definition: the response to request 2 arrives within the attempt

terms.name: final list
terms.path: reducer: results.requestId after the last event, read by search.adapter observe
terms.definition: the request whose results the list shows when the attempt ends

terms.name: late older result shown
terms.path: reducer: results.requestId after every event from response 1's late arrival on, read by search.adapter observe
terms.definition: a response to request 1 that arrived after request 2 was issued changed the list to request 1's results, at some step
terms.not: request 1's results kept on screen from before request 2 was issued (S1 item 1 keeps them)

terms.name: shown results intact
terms.path: reducer: results.items after every event, read through search.adapter snapshot, compared with the results the harness delivered with that response
terms.definition: after every event, the list displays exactly the results of the response it shows, and no results when it shows none

terms.name: older response empty
terms.path: test: the world adapter delivers response 1 with an empty result list
terms.definition: the response to request 1 carries no results; it is still request 1's response

terms.name: newer response empty
terms.path: test: the world adapter delivers response 2 with an empty result list
terms.definition: the response to request 2 carries no results; it is still the latest request's response (S1 item 3)

terms.name: long session
terms.path: test: the world adapter issues eight earlier requests, never answered, before the attempt, so the attempt's requests are 9 and 10
terms.definition: the attempt's requests are the ninth and tenth of the session, so their ids cross from one digit to two (9 and 10)
terms.not: responses to the earlier requests (they never arrive)

terms.name: list change
terms.definition: an event after which the list shows another request's results, other results, or nothing where it showed results
terms.not: issuing a request, after which the list keeps what it shows (S1 item 1)

hazards.permission-change: n/a: S1 no permission in the search policy
hazards.effect-count: n/a: S1 each response arrives at most once
hazards.identity-reference: n/a: S1 request ids are the only identity

contract.given: requests 1 and 2 issued; response 1 arrives before or after request 2 is issued
contract.then: the list ends with request 2's response, also when it carries no results
contract.never: the list ends without request 2's response
contract.bva: arrival: 1 before request 2, 1 then 2, 2 then 1; response 2 empty or not

contract.given: request 2 issued while request 1 is unanswered
contract.when: response 1 arrives, before or after response 2, empty or not
contract.then: a response to request 1 arriving after request 2 was issued never changes the list, at any step
contract.never: a late response to request 1 shown, even briefly
contract.bva: arrival: 1 then 2, 2 then 1; response 1 empty or not

contract.given: requests 1 and 2 issued; response 2 does not arrive
contract.when: response 1 arrives before or after request 2 is issued, or nothing arrives
contract.then: the list keeps showing what it showed when request 2 was issued: request 1's results when they had arrived, else nothing
contract.never: the kept results cleared, or request 1's late results shown
contract.sideEffects: results rendered×0 after request 2 is issued
contract.bva: response 2: withheld; response 1: before or after request 2

contract.then: the list displays exactly the results of the response it shows, or none
contract.never: results of no shown response, a mix of two responses, or a shown response without its own results
contract.bva: final: none, older, newer; results: empty or not; every event

contract.outside: trace conformance of the reducer on every trace of the Formal Model space (S2)
contract.given: every trace of up to 5 events that `Search.next` allows
contract.when: each event is applied to the reducer
contract.then: the reducer's observation equals `Search.observe` at every prefix
contract.never: a prefix where they differ; an adapter error or budget stop counted as a pass

notApplicable.text: loading indicator, error, timeout, retry, duplicate responses, cancellation and pagination are outside this fixture's policy; out-of-order arrival is the arrival axis and the Formal Model space

behavior.observation: `Search.observe` is the request id whose results the list shows, 0 when none; the adapter reads the reducer's `results.requestId`
behavior.outOfScope: cancellation, retry, duplicate responses, a response before its request (S1 item 4)

faultModel.note: the shown results lose their items
only the previous request counts as stale
a response appends to the results already shown

faultModel.replace: if (event.items.length === 0) return { ...state, results: null }; if (event.requestId !== state.latestRequestId) return state
faultModel.note: an empty response clears the list before the stale check
a stale response clears the list

faultModel.replace: if (event.requestId !== state.latestRequestId && (state.results === null || state.results.requestId === state.latestRequestId)) return state
faultModel.note: a late response is ignored only when nothing or the latest is shown

operators.dependency-failure: n/a: S1 errors, retry and cancellation are outside this fixture policy
operators.environment-variation: n/a: S1 a pure reducer with no browser, device or viewport in scope
operators.malformed-input: n/a: S1 request ids come from the product, not from user input

world.Race.itemsIntact.reason: space v1 let the mutant that empties the shown results (F5) survive every check: the observation was only the request id

world.Race.newEmpty.reason: no world delivered an empty response, so a product that skips empty responses passed every check of space v2

world.Race.oldEmpty.reason: no world delivered an empty late response, so an empty-response branch ahead of the stale check passed every check of space v2

world.Race.longSession.reason: the space never reached a two-digit request id (the traces stop at 4 events, sampling at 8), so comparing ids as text passed every check of space v3
